title: Battle HUD Feedback
author: Blatherbox
selftext: Just having some fun building a JRPG 2D pixel style game. I am looking for some feedback on my HUD. I am happy with the way it looks but it does limit the amount of screen I have for battles but I feel like it won't need more space than this. I have tried so many different variations with the characters on the left, with the menu and the characters to the right of the menu. I am torn because I like the menu a lot (currently only showing 3 skills but will eventually be limited to 6 that the player will have to choice from). Also for this fight the light source is from the lanterns so the Birdie and Daphne and the lower grub are a little dark but that's just this battle. Roland's holy energy sword is also a light source .. but I am asking about the HUD so guess those things don't matter. Any suggestions or mock ups people would like to share?

comments.author: 0bscuris
comments.body:
I think ur problem isn’t ur hud, it’s ur camera. 

Because the screen is so wide, at this level of zoom and angle, u end up with a bunch of dead space like between holy strike and the ap cost or between sewer worm and the turn predicator. 

Then, have even more dead space between the players and the wall behind them and the worms and wall behind them. 

Try offsetting the camera to the left or right a bit, so all the dead space is on one side and then move something to that side.

comments.author: Kanzes
comments.body: it's a bit of both i think hud kinda looks too busy with all the vibrant colors, since the game and sprite itself already vibrant. maybe try only a few selected tone and colors for hud

comments.author: Cute_Ad8981
comments.body:
My first impression on the image (even before reading your question) was: Ugh this is difficult to read.  

I would ask myself: Which UI elements are really needed? Does the player need to see each portrait? What elements to implemant, so that the player has all informations, which he needs?  

At the moment its hard to read essentiall things like hp for example. You have right and left a lot of dead space. background, characters and ui are all similar. Everything seams to detailed, so for example battlers blend into the background too much.  

These are just my opinions though.

comments.author: mrwolf214
comments.body: The buttons are so loooooonnnnnggggg.  Throw a picture of the UI at Claude Design and tell it you want it redone for ease of use and readability. Don’t settle for the first thing it shows you.  Tell it you want some flare, something unique.

comments.author: SanyaBane
comments.body: Take a look how Sengoku Rance display it's units on the battlefield. How unit cards located at the bottom and unit sprites are showing at top side of screen, with little to no animation.

comments.author: LittleLanternDev
comments.body:
Really nice art, the lantern lighting looks great! A few thoughts on the HUD:

**1. Show the menu only when it's needed.** Right now the action menu *and* the full party row are always visible, so the bottom \~30% of the screen is UI. You could collapse the party row into slim cards (portrait, HP/AP bar, no labels) and only expand the active character's card into the action menu, popping up right above their card. That frees a lot of space and makes it obvious whose turn it is.

**2. Six abilities fit in a 2×3 grid.** Name on the left, AP cost on the right, like you already do. That keeps the menu the same height when you go from 3 to 6 skills.

**3. Readability.** The small text on the party cards (HP/AP/UP) is hard to read at phone or Steam Deck size. Fewer numbers, bigger bars, and the number only on the bar that matters (HP) would help.

**4. Agree with Obscuris on the camera.** The fight sits in the middle with a lot of empty floor around it. Zooming in a bit, or shifting the camera so the fight sits just above the HUD, would make the battle feel bigger without changing the HUD at all.  
Target line ("Holy Heal → Daphne 30/190") and the turn order are great, I'd keep those exactly as they are!

comments.author: Blatherbox
comments.body: Thanks for all the feedback. I agree with most of it and will try a few different ideas. Thanks again.
